title: Quick to learn and valuable for collaborating
likes: Notion is a collaborative cloud-based tool combining the benefits of a database, tables, and word/images/file links. Aside from the ease of collaboration with colleagues, I really like the 'History' feature, where you can go back in time to a previous version of your Notion page to restore if you made changes you did not intend.
dislikes: Notion can be a bit clunky at first to learn. I suggest taking a quick tutorial before diving in. Although I learned it pretty quickly, there are features I didn't know upfront that would have been useful had I known them from the start. The tool is very powerful, so just a cursory understanding does not allow you to use the many benefits.
problemsSolved: Our teams work remotely, and we are using Notion as a centralized database of all sorts of information. We use this for documentation, sharing progress on projects, and more! Notion allows users to easy add simple notes, pages, tables, databases, images of all types, URL links and more - excellent for collaborating within 1 tool in the cloud.

title: A Flexible Home for Engineering Docs, Though Organization Takes Work
likes: Notion gives us one central place for our engineering docs instead of having them scattered across Google Docs, Slack threads and READMEs. Linking pages and using databases with templates keeps docs consistent and makes it easier to find past decisions and context. The flexible editor is the standout: I can write quickly with slash commands, markdown shortcuts, code blocks and toggles, and embed diagrams, tables and links. Templates give design docs and postmortems the right structure, and databases let us tag docs by project and status so it’s easy to see what’s current. Sharing and commenting make team reviews simple. Notion AI helps summarize long threads and find answers across the workspace, which makes onboarding faster because new engineers can find things themselves. Notion and its Slack integrations save us time, and embeds and link previews for Linear issues and Figma designs work well. We wanted one searchable, well-organized home that engineers and non-engineers could easily read and edit, and Notion fit that best. Setup was very easy: we were up and running in a day, importing Google Docs and markdown files worked well, and the built-in templates gave us a good starting point. Notion has become the home for our engineering knowledge, and I’d recommend it to other engineering teams.
dislikes: As our workspace grows, it can get messy with outdated pages and duplicate docs, so it takes discipline to keep things organized. Large pages and databases can feel slow to load. Code blocks could use better syntax highlighting, and I’d like deeper Git integration, including a native GitHub sync for docs that live alongside code. Offline support is also limited. I’d also love built-in tools to flag pages that haven’t been updated in a while.
problemsSolved: Notion gives our engineering team one central place for specs, design docs, runbooks, and onboarding notes instead of having them scattered across Google Docs, Slack threads, and READMEs. Linking pages and using database templates keeps our docs consistent and makes past decisions and context much easier to find.

title: A Flexible Hub for Connected, AI-Powered Workflows and Knowledge Management
likes: I use Notion to bring my agency’s workflows, data, and projects together and keep track of project status and outstanding tasks. I like how flexible it is—it let us make the system work the way we needed. The meeting transcription and summaries are super useful, and the flexible tables and databases have been amazing. I also really like how the MCP server ties Notion to AI agents. The templates and guidance were useful, and setup felt pretty intuitive and made it easy to get to the kind of AI enterprise-style solution I was aiming for pretty quickly.
dislikes: Notion’s customizability meant I had a bit of a learning curve to start with, but I found the templates and guidance useful.
problemsSolved: I use Notion to improve visibility across platforms, understand where projects stand and what they need, and keep outstanding tasks mentioned in meetings from getting lost. It also helps create a shared understanding across the organization.
